title: Geometric Frobenius pullback and internal Hom at every coefficient stage
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a chosen algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $g=g_\gamma=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ with $\gamma(z)=z^{1/q}$, the geometric-Frobenius automorphism [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Work on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

Let $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, and let $M,N\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with $M$ site-perfect [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Write $H_\Lambda(M,N)=R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_X}(M,N)$, using the operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. At $\mathcal O_E$, $\Lambda_X=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_X$, $Lg^*$ is the completed pullback defined as the derived inverse limit of the finite pullbacks, and $H_\Lambda$ is the ambient ringed-site internal Hom over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$, exactly as in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. The integral tensor below is completed derived tensor. At $E$ use scalar localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use the common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

Let $\mu$ be the specified pullback-tensor isomorphism of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] and $\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}:M\otimes^L H_\Lambda(M,N)\to N$ the counit of the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction [sk-def-sf-operations] (i). Define $\alpha_{g;M,N}$ to be the transpose under that adjunction of
$$
 Lg^*M\otimes^L Lg^*H_\Lambda(M,N)
 \xrightarrow{\ \mu_{g;M,H_\Lambda(M,N)}^{-1}\ }
 Lg^*(M\otimes^L H_\Lambda(M,N))
 \xrightarrow{\ Lg^*(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N})\ }Lg^*N.
$$
Then this specified comparison is an isomorphism
$$
 \alpha_{g;M,N}:Lg^*R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_X}(M,N)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_X}(Lg^*M,Lg^*N).
$$
It is natural contravariantly in $M$ and covariantly in $N$, with the displayed evaluation identity. At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ it is the canonical comparison of [thm-trf-internal-hom-pullback]. At $\mathcal O_E$ its derived reduction modulo $\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], under the canonical reduction comparisons for pullback and internal Hom of [lem-fix-operation-reduction], is $\alpha_{g;M_n,N_n}$, where $M_n=M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ and similarly for $N_n$; these identifications commute with successive quotient reductions. The rational comparison is the image of the integral comparison on integral representatives, extended to the localized category. For a finite extension $E\subset L$ these comparisons commute with the pullback and internal-Hom scalar-extension identifications of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] and their rationalizations, compatibly with identity and successive field extension. In particular their common-stage classes are independent of the finite field of definition.

proof.text: Set $F=Lg^*$ and $H=R\mathcal Hom$. At finite coefficients we use the ambient derived category and its adjunction $M\otimes^L-\dashv H(M,-)$, as in [sk-def-sf-operations] (i). At integral coefficients work first on the full category $\mathcal C=D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$, even without site-perfectness of either input. By [cor-coef-integral-internal-hom], $H(M,N)$ lies in $\mathcal C$ for all $M,N\in\mathcal C$. By [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], $F$ and completed tensor preserve $\mathcal C$. The completed tensor-Hom adjunction on this full category is the natural bijection of [lem-coef-completed-tensor-hom-transpose]. Thus all terms of the displayed definition of $\alpha$ and its transpose are in the required categories; in particular $\mu_{g;M,H(M,N)}$ is defined. The integral Hom here is the ambient Hom over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$, and the tensor in this adjunction is completed tensor.

proof.text: The morphism $g$ is the scheme automorphism of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], with inverse induced by $z\mapsto z^q$. At finite coefficients $F$ is an equivalence on the ambient derived category by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-equivalence]. At integral coefficients apply [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] to both $g$ and its inverse. It identifies their completed pullbacks, naturally on $\mathcal C$, with the two termwise inverse-image transports. To check their inverse identities, use the site equivalences of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (1): relabelling $U\to X$ by $g$ and then by $g^{-1}$ returns that object and every restriction map. Clause (3), followed by the limit comparison of clause (2), identifies the completed coefficient ring with its relabelling. Transporting a module action and then transporting it back therefore returns the same action and module map. These inverse identities hold degreewise on complexes, and hence after localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Both transports preserve the full constructible integral subcategories by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]. Consequently $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ is an equivalence. No $k$-linearity of $g$ is required by these scheme-isomorphism lemmas.

proof.text: Fix $M$ and apply [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] with $L=M\otimes^L-$, $R=H(M,-)$, $L'=FM\otimes^L-$, $R'=H(FM,-)$, $G=G'=F$, and $\theta_T=\mu_{g;M,T}^{-1}:FM\otimes^L FT\to F(M\otimes^L T)$. The natural tensor isomorphism is supplied by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Step 2 verifies both equivalence hypotheses. The mate's component at $N$ is the transpose of $F(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N})\mu_{g;M,H(M,N)}^{-1}$: this is exactly the unit--$R'\theta R$--$R'F\operatorname{ev}$ formula in the cited lemma. It is therefore the specified $\alpha_{g;M,N}$, and is invertible. This argument applies to arbitrary finite ambient pairs and arbitrary integral constructible pairs, not only to the site-perfect pairs required by the item. In the stated finite site-perfect case the canonical comparison of [thm-trf-internal-hom-pullback] is this evaluation transpose, so it is the same map. All adjunctions used here are those of Step 1, rather than an adjunction on an unproved subcategory.

proof.text:
The defining transpose gives the evaluation identity
$$\operatorname{ev}_{FM,FN}(1_{FM}\otimes^L\alpha_{M,N})=F(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N})\mu_{g;M,H(M,N)}^{-1}.$$
For $a:M'\to M$ and $b:N\to N'$, compare $H(Fa,Fb)\alpha_{M,N}$ and $\alpha_{M',N'}F(H(a,b))$. Uncurrying both, naturality of evaluation and of $\mu$ makes each the map
$$FM'\otimes^L F H(M,N)\xrightarrow{Fa\otimes1}FM\otimes^L F H(M,N)\xrightarrow{\mu^{-1}}F(M\otimes^L H(M,N))\xrightarrow{F\operatorname{ev}}FN\xrightarrow{Fb}FN'.$$
Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves equality. This proves the two asserted variances at finite and integral coefficients without changing the chosen comparison.

proof.text:
For integral coefficients let $R_n$ denote derived reduction. Write $\rho_T:R_nFT\xrightarrow{\sim}F_nR_nT$ and $\beta_{A,B}:R_nH(A,B)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_n(R_nA,R_nB)$ for the canonical comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Set
$$r_n=F_n(\beta_{M,N})\rho_{H(M,N)},\qquad b_n=H_n(\rho_M^{-1},\rho_N)\beta_{FM,FN}.$$
Then the precise reduction assertion is
$$b_nR_n(\alpha_{M,N})=\alpha_{M_n,N_n}r_n.$$
To prove it, uncurry in the finite category. The preservation of evaluation in [lem-fix-operation-reduction] replaces $R_n\operatorname{ev}$ by $\operatorname{ev}_n$; the reduction compatibility of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] replaces $R_n\mu^{-1}$ by $\mu_n^{-1}$. Both uncurried sides are consequently the reduction of the pairing $F(\operatorname{ev})\mu^{-1}$, with its first input identified by $\rho_M$. The finite adjunction in [sk-def-sf-operations] gives the equation. This uses the integral-to-finite Hom comparison, whose statement imposes no perfectness restriction. For successive-quotient compatibility, [def-weil-site-perfect-complex] shows that reducing a bounded local finite-projective complex preserves its split idempotents; pulling it back does the same, by the tensor unit and finite-sum comparisons. Thus the finite first inputs remain site-perfect. Apply the finite-quotient comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] to $A_{E,m}\to A_{E,n}$. The direct and successive Hom comparisons are both transposes of the same successively reduced evaluation, by the associative tensor comparisons in that lemma. Uniqueness of transpose identifies them, and identifies the two reduced $\alpha$ equations. This proves compatibility with every successive quotient, without assuming those quotient maps are flat.

proof.text: Rationalize the integral natural isomorphism of Step 3 on all of $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ using [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Its image is invertible because the images of its inverse satisfy the two inverse identities. These are exactly the rational operations on objects and morphisms specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The rational tensor-Hom bijection of [lem-coef-completed-tensor-hom-transpose] identifies the rationalized evaluation equation of Step 4 with the defining equation for $\alpha$ over $E$; uniqueness of transpose proves that it is the specified rational map. Naturality holds for every rational morphism: express a morphism as an integral morphism times a power of $\varpi_E^{-1}$, apply integral naturality and linearity in each variable. This treats all rational objects, since the localization has the same objects. In particular it does not assume that an arbitrary integral representative of a rational site-perfect object is itself site-perfect.

proof.text:
Let $T=-\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$. Denote the pullback comparison by $\rho_A:TF_EA\xrightarrow{\sim}F_LTA$, and the internal-Hom comparison by $\beta_{A,B}:TH_E(A,B)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_L(TA,TB)$, as in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. Define
$$r_T=F_L(\beta_{M,N})\rho_{H_E(M,N)},\qquad b_T=H_L(\rho_M^{-1},\rho_N)\beta_{F_EM,F_EN}.$$
The required scalar square is
$$b_TT(\alpha_E)=\alpha_Lr_T.$$
Apply [lem-coef-monoidal-square-hom-transport] with its horizontal functors $F_E,F_L$ and vertical functors both $T$; its square is $\rho^{-1}:F_LT\cong TF_E$. Its hypotheses hold: [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] supplies the strong symmetric tensor structures and their compatibility with scalar change; [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] supplies the natural isomorphisms; [lem-fix-operation-reduction] states that the coefficient comparisons preserve tensor associativity, evaluation, units and counits. Thus the internal-Hom comparisons are the evaluation-defined ones required by the square lemma, and its displayed identity is precisely the equation above. Equivalently, uncurrying gives $TF_E(\operatorname{ev})$ after the same inverse tensor comparisons on each side. For $L=E$ these identifications are identities. For $E\subset L\subset L'$ the composition identifications of the scalar-extension lemma and the tensor coherence identify the direct square with the pasted squares; their middle comparisons and inverses cancel. This proves identity and successive-extension compatibility as identities of the specified maps. Rationalizing this equation proves the same assertion for the rationalizations of these comparisons.

proof.text: Represent $M,N$ and the finitely many arrows in a naturality or evaluation equation over one common finite coefficient field, as permitted by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Define the common-stage comparison by the class of the rational $\alpha$ over that field. Step 7 says that extending the field carries this representative to the specified comparison over the larger field. Two choices therefore agree over their compositum and define the same class. The class of the rational inverse is its inverse, since both compositions are the identity at that common field. The formulas for the common-stage operations in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] now identify this class with the comparison in the question: its uncurried pairing is the class of $F(\operatorname{ev})\mu^{-1}$. The evaluation identity and naturality of Step 4 hold as common-stage identities, and the identity and successive-extension identities of Step 7 show independence of the finite field of definition.
